item.title: 2027: Ogun indigenes rally behind Adebutu, reaffirm ‘Ogun for Ogun’ agenda
item.description: .pledge grassroots mobilisation as PDP candidate takes campaign to communities By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Indigenes of Ogun State have reaffirmed their commitment to protecting the state’s political heritage, declaring support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ movement ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The residents made the pledge during separate engagements at the ward-to-ward campaign tours of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, across the state’s local government areas. The campaign tour, which has taken Adebutu and Kolapo to various communities in recent weeks, is aimed at mobilising grassroots support for the PDP candidates and presenting their seven-point development agenda, tagged ITURA DE, to the electorate. At the different ward meetings, residents, community leaders, market women, farmers and youths turned out to welcome the candidates, with several communities receiving them with colourful displays and enthusiastic celebrations. The engagements also provided opportunities for residents to interact directly with the candidates, raise concerns about their communities and outline their expectations from the next administration. Among the major issues raised were the poor condition of rural roads, unemployment, inadequate agricultural support and the need for improved infrastructure and access to modern farming equipment. Several stakeholders pledged to mobilise support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, arguing that the state’s leadership should reflect the interests, heritage and aspirations of its indigenes. At Alagada Ward in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a market leader, Mrs Folasade Ogunye, said her support for the movement was informed by the belief that indigenous leadership would better understand the challenges confronting grassroots communities. She lamented the poor condition of roads leading to markets and the limited employment opportunities available to young people, insisting that residents needed a leader who understood their everyday struggles. “We, the women of Obafemi/Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad, and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and understands our struggles. “We believe that someone with a genuine connection to the people will better appreciate our challenges. That is why we have pledged to go from house to house to mobilise support for this mandate. It is about our pride and the future of Ogun indigenes,” she said. In a related development, some residents said to be former members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at Alapakooni community in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area publicly renounced their allegiance to the party. The defectors reportedly set bunches of APC brooms ablaze to symbolise their departure from the party, citing dissatisfaction with its political leadership and questions surrounding the identity of its governorship

item.title: FG policies raise Nigeria’s exports by 25% – Dantsoho
item.description: Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), says Federal Government policies and reforms have increased Nigeria’s exports by 25 per cent in the last two years. Dantsoho said this on Tuesday at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH) in London. Mr Ikechukwu Onyemekara, NPA’s General Manager, Corporate Communication and Strategy, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen in Lagos. Dantsoho said that Nigeria’s large population offered the country significant economic advantages, while recent reforms had contributed to increased cargo throughput and export volumes. He said that the growth covered not only oil and gas but also manufactured goods, agricultural products, including cocoa and cashew, as well as raw materials. He attributed the development to improved collaboration between the NPA and major terminal operators, including APM Terminals, which had enhanced operational efficiency, export volumes and port competitiveness. The NPA boss said that the authority had established about four Export Processing Terminals to streamline export operations. He explained that the terminals operated in collaboration with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargo was processed locally before shipment. According to him, the arrangement ensures that Nigerian export products meet international standards and reduces challenges associated with quality compliance in destination markets. Dantsoho said that Nigeria was better positioned to benefit from the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) through the reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu. He said that the reforms had strengthened the economy and attracted investors, creating opportunities for increased trade and cooperation among African countries. He cited Nigeria’s growing trade relations with Morocco, particularly in the manufacturing sector, noting that the North African country had emerged as a hub for electric vehicle and smaller vehicle production. Dantsoho also attributed Nigeria’s improved global port ranking to the reforms, noting that two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking. He described the achievement as a result of improved efficiency, technology adoption and effective collaboration with industry stakeholders. The NPA managing director further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, driven by increased cargo volumes and partnerships with international investors and terminal operators. He said that Nigerian ports had recorded significant improvements in efficiency compared with other ports in West Africa. item.title: Ballot machine glitch hits New York county in tight House race
item.description: Ballot machines malfunctioned in a hotly contested House race in New York state Tuesday, prompting right-wing influencers to fling unfounded allegations of US midterms voter fraud even as local election officials insisted all ballots would be counted. President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven claims about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable. The Westchester County Board of Elections said it was aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county. The board “wants to reassure every voter that your vote matters, your ballot will be secure and your vote will be counted,” with ballots instead placed in emergency bags, it said in a statement. Parts of Westchester County are included in New York’s 17th district, where incumbent Republican Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in a House of Representatives seat that voted for Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. Pro-Donald Trump influencers pounced on the glitch by claiming, without evidence, that Democrats were trying to “steal” the election. They included conspiracy theorist Laura Loomer, conservative activist Scott Pressler, and Katie Miller, a podcaster married to White House advisor Stephen Miller. The New York State Board of Elections said on X that there has been no disruption to voting. “Long-established emergency ballot procedures have been implemented, where completed ballots are secured, under bipartisan control, and will be counted,” it said. The Board added in a later statement that the technical error was linked to voting machines being unable to read and accept the ballots. “Importantly, the affected scanners rejected ballots they could not properly recognize rather than incorrectly tabulating them,” it said. item.title: APC rejects Tinubu campaign council list in Osun, demands review
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun has rejected its State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) list, alleging breaches of party guidelines and exclusion of key officials. Mr Wole Adunola, Osun APC Publicity Secretary, disclosed this in a statement jointly signed by two other party officials on Tuesday in Abuja. Adunola said the list failed to reflect due process, inclusiveness and respect for established party structures. He said the exclusion of several State Working Committee members, who should be statutory members, informed the rejection. “Of particular concern is the omission of several members of the State Working Committee who, according to applicable guidelines, are expected to be statutory members of the council,” he said. Adunola said the exclusion raised concerns about consultation, due process and respect for the party’s established leadership structure. He also questioned the composition of the council in relation to an earlier presidential directive reportedly naming Gov. Ademola Adeleke as its Director-General. According to him, Adeleke subsequently inaugurated a broad-based campaign team to coordinate President Bola Tinubu’s presidential campaign across the state. Adunola said it was unclear why a different structure had emerged without adequate clarification or alignment with the existing arrangement. He suggested that the newly released list might have been intended for a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the PCC. “If the newly released list was intended to serve as a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the PCC, its composition would be more understandable,” he said. Adunola said the distinction must be clarified to prevent confusion, duplication of responsibilities and unnecessary friction within the party’s campaign structure. He stressed that the State Executive Committee remained integral to the APC’s organisational framework and should not be sidelined. “A successful campaign must be built on mutual respect, proper coordination, and the active involvement of legitimate party stakeholders,” he said. Adunola called for an immediate review of the list, with consultations involving relevant stakeholders, including APC National Secretary, Sen. Surajudeen Basiru, and the State Director-General. He said the consultations would ensure proper alignment, effective coordination and respect for established party procedures. Adunola reaffirmed the chapter’s commitment to Tinubu’s re-election bid and the overall interests of the APC. He, however, warned that party loyalty should not prevent constructive engagement when decisions risk creating avoidable divisions and undermining collective efforts. He urged party leaders at state and national levels to address the concerns promptly and make the necessary corrections. Adunola said an effective campaign council must accommodate legitimate stakeholders, recognise established leadership and unite members towards electoral victory. item.title: Olodo murder: Police arrest two suspects, deploy Army, Amotekun
item.description: .as tension grips Ibadan community By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the killing of a 26-year-old man, identified as Kehinde Asimiyu, following a fatal altercation at Olodo Garage in the Lagelu Local Government Area of Ibadan, while reinforcing security in the area to prevent a breakdown of law and order. The development came amid heightened tension in the Olodo community following the fatal stabbing of the young man, popularly known as KBlaq, by a commercial motorcyclist during a disagreement over transport fare, an incident that disrupted commercial activities and forced residents and commuters to trek considerable distances after motorcycle operators withdrew their services over fears of possible reprisal attacks. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said the command received a report of the incident on 1 November 2026, indicating that the deceased had allegedly been stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde following an altercation between the two men at Olodo Garage. According to the police, “the deceased was allegedly stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde at Olodo Garage following an altercation between both parties.” The statement added that the incident subsequently came to the attention of the deceased’s family when “an unidentified motorcycle rider arrived at their residence and informed them of the attack.” “Following receipt of the report, police operatives, accompanied by a patrol team, immediately mobilised to the scene, while the victim was rushed to Academy Hospital, Texaco, Iwo Road, Ibadan, where he was confirmed dead by the doctor on duty.“ “His remains were subsequently deposited at Adejare Embalming Centre for preservation, while photographs were taken as part of the preliminary investigative procedures.“ The police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the killing had led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as Taiwo Babarinde, suspected to have inflicted the fatal injury on the deceased, and Ishola Semiu, suspected of involvement in the incident. “Both suspects are currently in Police custody, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for comprehensive investigation,” the statement said. However, the police intervention following the killing also witnessed a fresh security challenge, as unrest reportedly erupted at the Olodo Police Outpost, nearly resulting in a breakdown of law and order. The situation was further compounded by subsequent reports of threats from hoodlums, prompting the immediate reinforcement of security across the area to prevent further disturbances and protect residents. item.title: Ogun govt, Ijebu Chiefs clash over Awujale Council as succession crisis deepens
item.description: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta A fresh controversy has erupted over the administration of Ijebuland following the decision of the Ogun State government to reconstitute the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), barely a day after traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode announced the dissolution of the council and its replacement with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The development has exposed a disagreement between the state government and some traditional authorities over the appropriate legal and customary structure for administering Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale. While the government insists that the AIAC remains the only legally recognised administrative body authorised to oversee the affairs of Ijebuland during the interregnum, the traditional chiefs maintain that the Adele Oba Awujale in Council is rooted in the customs and established traditional practices of the Ijebu people. In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat, the state government said the withdrawal of some members of the AIAC did not invalidate the council or confer legal authority on another body to take over its responsibilities. The government described the AIAC, established in August 2025, as the only legally recognised administrative structure empowered to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland until a new Awujale is appointed and crowned. It specifically clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal from the council. Dismissing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, the government maintained that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy laws of Ogun State. According to Hamzat, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the administration of the vacant Awujale stool. The government also faulted the reliance on the Chiefs Law of 1957 by some former members to justify the emergence of the new body, arguing that the legislation was enacted before Nigeria’s independence and no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976. To support its position, the state government cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others. item.title: Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards
item.description: The Federal Government has paid cash rewards to players, coaches and officials of the Super Falcons following their victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), completing the reward package promised by President Bola Tinubu. The National Sports Commission (NSC) disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Head of Press and Public Relations, Zira Zakka Nagga. According to the commission, each player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while each coach and official received the equivalent of $50,000. The team had earlier received the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) and three-bedroom apartments. The Chairman of the NSC, Shehu Dikko, thanked Tinubu for fulfilling his pledge, saying the President had directed that all aspects of the reward package be delivered within a reasonable time. “The Super Falcons made Nigeria proud, and Mr President has honoured his commitment to them in full. This means a great deal to the team and to Nigerian sports,” Dikko said. He said the President’s action marked a departure from previous experiences in which some Nigerian athletes waited years to receive promised rewards. “Some of our sports heroes endured years of waiting for promises to be fulfilled. President Tinubu has shown that things can be done differently,” he said. Dikko added that the fulfilment of the pledge would encourage athletes to represent the country with confidence that their efforts would be recognised. He also said the gesture would inspire young Nigerians, particularly girls aspiring to pursue careers in sports. The NSC chairman recalled that Nigeria’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress, received similar cash rewards in September 2026 after winning their fifth consecutive FIBA Women’s AfroBasket title in 2025. Each D’Tigress player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while officials received $50,000 each. The team had also received three-bedroom apartments and national honours. Dikko also cited the completion of rewards for the Super Eagles following their silver-medal finish at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations, held in Côte d’Ivoire in 2024. He thanked the Ministers of Finance, Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, and Housing and Urban Development for their roles in completing the reward package. “Delivering these rewards required close cooperation across government. We appreciate the Honourable Ministers and their teams for working with the Commission to complete the necessary processes,” he said. The commission congratulated the Super Falcons’ players, coaches and officials on their achievement, urging Nigerian athletes preparing for future competitions to draw encouragement from the fulfilment of the President’s promises. It quoted Tinubu as saying: “My promise to every Nigerian athlete is: make Nigeria proud, and come back to a grateful nation.” The post Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Atiku Alleges Plot To Disrupt ADC Campaign In Sokoto, Vows Resistance
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of working to frustrate the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in the state, alleging that protesters were being mobilised to disrupt the party’s planned rally. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. He described the strategy as one of political absorption and intimidation, warning that its ultimate objective was to leave Nigeria with little meaningful opposition. “The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name,” he said. Atiku also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the economy, pointing to the rising prices of food, transport, fuel and electricity as evidence of the pressure on households. He said the ADC would pursue policies aimed at expanding local production, increasing food supply, generating employment and lowering the cost of doing business if elected in 2027. Among his proposals is a targeted production subsidy linked to fuel refined in Nigeria. He said the measure would ease the burden on consumers while supporting domestic industry. item.title: Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi State. The operation took place on Tuesday in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela-Odolu Local Government Area, as troops continued efforts to track fleeing suspects following a raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the same forest on Monday. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lt. Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Lokoja. Abdullahi said troops sustained their operations in the forest to locate fleeing suspects, clear remaining hideouts and restrict the movement of criminal elements. He said the troops made contact with the suspects during the follow-up operation and engaged them, forcing them to retreat. “The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of two kidnappers, while others fled into the surrounding forest,” he said. A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, 438 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition and 4,725 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered included two bandoliers, two mobile phones and a power bank. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that troops had dismantled a suspected kidnappers’ camp in the forest during Monday’s operation, recovering about 1,000 rounds of ammunition and six motorcycles. Abdullahi said Tuesday’s operation had consolidated the gains of the earlier raid, adding that troops remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal groups. He said the brigade would continue operations to protect lives and property and support efforts to restore lasting peace across Kogi State. item.title: Toluwanisings: Oyo Police summon wife, father, friends as parties sign peace deal
item.description: The Oyo State Police Command has brokered peace between the family and associates of late Nigerian singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, following disagreements over his burial arrangements. The intervention comes amid allegations of conspiracy, defamation of character and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace, which reportedly generated public exchanges between parties on social media and other communication platforms. In a statement on Tuesday, the Command said the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received information about the dispute on October 28, 2026, and subsequently directed the parties to appear at the Command Headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, for an intervention. The police said the meeting, which was held on November 3, resulted in the parties signing a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. Those involved included the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as his personal assistant and other representatives. According to the statement, the parties agreed to maintain peace, exhibit good behaviour and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions surrounding the singer’s death and burial arrangements. The statement reads, “Consequently, at the conclusion of the engagement held today, 3rd November 2026, all parties, comprising the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as the deceased’s personal assistant and other representatives, entered into and signed a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. “Under the terms of the undertaking, all parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace, and discontinue public exchanges, interviews and discussions capable of inflaming tensions or aggravating the existing disagreement surrounding the unfortunate demise of the singer and related issues. “Furthermore, the parties expressly undertook to discontinue the dissemination of information, narratives, allegations and publications relating to the matter through social media platforms, print media, radio, blogs and other communication channels, including publications made through their respective proxies, agents, associates and representatives. They equally agreed not to grant interviews, provide access or facilitate engagements with individuals or media platforms for the purpose of further disseminating such narratives. item.title: NBS: Enugu records lowest tax Revenue-to-IGR ratio
item.description: …Abia, FCT, Bayelsa top tax-heavy IGR states Enugu State recorded the lowest tax revenue-to-Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) ratio in 2025, StatiSense has said, quoting figures from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). According to statistics published on StatiSense’s verified X handle, only N51.52 billion, or 12.67 per cent of the N406.7 billion in IGR generated by Enugu State in 2025, came from tax revenues, while the rest came from non-tax revenues. Recall that the NBS had earlier in the year rated Enugu State as number one in IGR growth among the 36 states and the FCT, coming only behind Lagos and Rivers States, in that order. However, in terms of the tax component of IGR, the state recorded the lowest tax-to-IGR ratio, while Abia State led with 100 per cent of its N70.41 billion IGR in 2025 coming from taxes. Abia was followed by the FCT, which had 100 per cent of its N356.34 billion 2025 IGR coming from tax revenues. Bayelsa (99.39 per cent), Rivers (96.72 per cent) and Sokoto (92.44 per cent) make up the top five tax-dependent states for IGR. But joining Governor Peter Mbah’s Enugu on the list of states with the least tax dependence for IGR are Kwara (38.42 per cent), Katsina (39.93 per cent), Osun (41.53 per cent) and Ogun (44.10 per cent). At a recent town hall in Enugu, televised live by some national television stations, Governor Peter Mbah had dismissed the narrative that his administration was overtaxing the people, noting that it was being fuelled by the opposition and beneficiaries of the corruption and sharp practices that prevailed in the revenue collection system until his administration came on board and implemented reforms, introducing technology in the process to plug revenue leakages. Mbah also maintained that, contrary to perception, the surge in the state’s revenue was driven by innovation and economic diversification under his administration, which had expanded revenue sources. He also reminded the audience that taxation was on the Exclusive Legislative List of the Constitution; hence, no state could legislate to increase or lower any form of tax, be it Personal Income Tax, Company Income Tax, Value Added Tax, Withholding Tax, among others. He said his administration had widened the tax net to bring in more people who had never paid tax, but had never increased taxes. “This is one falsehood that has been so peddled that it’s even beginning to take a semblance of a truth. Meanwhile, overtaxation does not exist, and I think those who think we may be taxing more are essentially looking at the sort of growth we have recorded in our IGR. “Because they couldn’t have imagined such growth happening within the period it happened, they felt perhaps the only justification is that we have burdened the people of Enugu to realise that. item.title: We’re ready for 2027 elections – IGP Disu
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has assured Nigerians that the Nigeria Police Force is fully prepared to provide security for the 2027 general elections even if it were to commence tomorrow. Disu gave the assurance on Tuesday during a meeting with the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel, Dr Leonardo Santos Simão, at the Force Headquarters in Abuja. According to him, the force had intensified the training and retraining of officers to strengthen their capacity to manage election-related security challenges and ensure professionalism throughout the electoral process. The IGP noted that the police had drawn lessons from recent off-cycle elections and identified areas requiring improvement. He added that the force was working closely with other security agencies, including the Nigerian Army, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Customs Service, Nigeria Immigration Service and Department of State Services, to ensure effective election security. Disu also disclosed that officers had received training on how to identify and assist persons with disabilities during elections. “We are not afraid. We are confident that even if the elections start tomorrow, the Nigerian police is ready to do what is expected of the Nigerian police,” he said. He assured Nigerians that the force would not disappoint in its responsibility to maintain law and order before, during and after the elections. Furthermore, the Police hierarchy disclosed that threat assessments has been carried out in zones and states of possible violence based on intelligence and how to nip the violence in the mud before they occur noting that increased deployments of personnel and assets will be enabled to ensure hitch-free voting exercise. Earlier, Simão emphasised the importance of the police in preserving peace and stability, particularly in a country facing security challenges, including terrorism. He urged the police to maintain neutrality and professionalism during elections, warning against actions that could undermine public confidence in the electoral process. item.title: Binance reveals hackers used fake job interviews, malicious code in $6-bn heist
item.description: Binance released on Tuesday a detailed investigation into the $6 billion hack of its cryptocurrency platform, showing how attackers used fake job interviews and malicious code to steal the funds. The crypto exchange said it had replenished 98 percent of the affected assets by drawing on its own funds, with the remaining amount involving little-traded currencies that are harder to acquire. The attack, carried out over about four hours on October 29, was attributed by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to North Korea-affiliated hackers. Pyongyang has denied the allegations, with the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un calling the claim “absurd rhetoric.” Around $2.85 billion of the stolen $6.34 billion has been frozen, Binance said, meaning that the attackers could not use it or convert it to another currency. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack, which is thought to be the biggest ever crypto heist, caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply. According to Binance, attackers took their first steps towards the breach as early as June. First, they targeted a platform engineer by getting them to download a virus-laden version of the widely-known programming software Homebrew. Binance’s cybersecurity teams identified the malware and removed it, but the hackers had already had time to harvest information about the engineer and his colleagues. In September, the attackers approached another Binance engineer through a legitimate job-search platform, offering him an interview for a position in a fictitious company. After building trust with the subject through the sharing of social media photos and videos, they asked the engineer to download a test exercise as part of the interview process. The exercise contained malware that deployed “sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques,” Binance said, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version. That malware was critical to the success of the attack, as it allowed the hackers to establish a connection with Binance’s internal systems. On October 20, the attackers used the access they had gained and an internal AI tool to gain control over software used by two other engineers. Nine days later, they triggered malicious code that initiated the attack. The post Binance reveals hackers used fake job interviews, malicious code in $6-bn heist appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Don’t oppress with your privilege — Makinde tells elites
item.description: Gov. Seyi Makinde has urged privileged and influential Nigerians to use their resources to uplift society rather than oppress others. Makinde made the call on Tuesday in Ibadan during the inauguration of the Joseph and Esther Homes for Senior Citizens. The inauguration also included the launch of a book, ‘Built from the Break’, authored by renowned Nollywood actress Shola Shobowale. The governor congratulated Shobowale, the founder of the home, describing her vision as quiet but deeply impactful. He said the initiative, which provides a safe, secure and dignified environment for the elderly, reinforces the traditional African value of caring for parents and senior citizens. He described the home as an extraordinary gesture inspired by Shobowale’s love for her parents and concern for the elderly. He noted that while public attention often gravitates toward large and visible projects, initiatives that directly improve lives often have the most enduring impact. Makinde also commended the actress for writing the book, noting that publishing a book requires courage, discipline and commitment. He announced that the access road to the home would be rehabilitated and fitted with solar-powered streetlights to improve accessibility and comfort for the home’s residents. item.title: PDP chairmen threaten action over killings, harassment of candidates
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Forum of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) State Chairmen has threatened to take action against governors accused of harassing, intimidating and killing the party’s candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. The state chairmen warned that they would no longer tolerate attacks on their candidates, insisting that political contests must not become an excuse for violence, intimidation or murder. Chairman of the forum, Hon. Austin Nwachukwu, gave the warning on Tuesday during a meeting of the PDP National Working Committee, NWC, with state chairmen at the party’s national secretariat in Abuja. Nwachukwu disclosed that the forum had been forced to intervene in Ebonyi State over alleged intimidation, harassment, arrests and killings of PDP candidates, accusing the state government of allowing the situation to persist. He said the forum was submitting a petition to the Inspector-General of Police and other relevant security agencies over the alleged attacks. “The killings and harassment of our candidates and governorship candidates, especially in various states of the country, must stop. “The forum will not take it lightly anymore if any of our candidates are harassed, intimidated or killed because of mere elections. It’s a contest. Winner must emerge,” Nwachukwu said. He expressed concern that some governors were allegedly antagonising PDP candidates despite the party’s painstaking efforts to produce candidates for the forthcoming elections. The forum chairman pledged the state chairmen’s support for the party’s national leadership, saying they were ready to work towards securing victory for the PDP in 2027. He said 36 state chairmen, including the FCT, attended the meeting, describing their presence as a demonstration of the forum’s commitment to the party. In his remarks, PDP National Chairman, Abdulrahman Mohammed, said the party’s internal processes would remain guided by its constitution and established traditions, including caucus meetings and expanded national meetings. Mohammed commended state chairmen for conducting nomination processes for candidates seeking election into state assemblies, the House of Representatives, Senate and governorship positions across the 36 states. He said the NWC would work with other party organs to ensure victory for the PDP in the 2027 elections, expressing confidence that the party’s performance would contribute to the country’s progress. The national chairman also appreciated members of the NWC for their support and contributions, urging them to remain united as the party prepares for the elections. item.title: Seen And Heard At The US Midterm Elections
item.description: Reporters, photographers and video journalists are deployed by AFP across the United States to document the 2026 midterm elections as Americans head to the polls. Here is a round-up of interviews on Tuesday at polling stations where voters agreed to share their thoughts about what was on their minds and motivating their choices. Hopeful Democrats With polling data suggesting the Democratic Party is on track to capture a majority in the House of Representatives and perhaps even in the Senate, many left-leaning voters said they were hopeful about the results. “Two years ago was a really devastating outcome for me,” Emma Mondadori, a 39-year-old who works in philanthropy, told AFP in Brooklyn, New York, referring to President Donald Trump’s election. “I’ve been really looking forward to this day where we get to have a say again in the future of our country… I’m cautiously hopeful, optimistic.” AUSTIN, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 03: Voters wait in line to cast their ballots at the polling place at the Baker Center on November 03, 2026 in Austin, Texas. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by CHIP SOMODEVILLA / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) The cost of living With gasoline prices up by a third since last year and diesel nearly double — not to mention sharp food price inflation — everyday spending was on many people’s minds. “It’s about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things. It needs to change for the everyday person, and I’m an everyday person,” Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in Atlanta, Georgia, told AFP. Tom, a 27-year-old businessman at the same polling station who declined to give his surname, agreed. “Everyone, at least in my generation, is a little frustrated with the affordability crisis and gas prices and what’s going on abroad,” added the non-partisan voter. Leadership referendum Mid-term elections are typically seen as a form of referendum on the sitting president. And few leaders have polarized public opinion as strongly as Donald Trump. “I’m independent but I voted Democrat, I just wanted to go back into the culture of decency, integrity, honesty, and the rest follows,” Yan Cardineau, 59, told AFP in Austin, Texas. “If we lose that, it doesn’t matter how much money you make.” Atlantans head to the polls to vote on Election Day at Park Tavern on November 3, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Megan Varner/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Megan Varner / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) Estrella Roque, a 69-year-old voter of Cuban origin, told AFP in Miami she had voted Republican. “What I like about the Republicans is that they can fix the country,” she explained in Spanish. “Donald Trump hasn’t been given time to show who he really is.” Immigration In his final pitch to voters, Trump has stressed his success in reducing immigration and stopping crossings along the southern border with Mexico. While his tough stance plays well with his core supporters, others have been put off by the brutal tactics

item.title: Don’t allow opposition criticism to distract you – APC to supporters
item.description: ‎ ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎A member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Musa Illiyasu Kwankwaso, has urged supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the North to remain focused and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso cautioned party members against being distracted by criticism from opposition groups, insisting that such attacks would not weaken the President’s political support base in northern Nigeria. ‎ ‎He made the call on Tuesday while reacting to opposition criticism of the Tinubu administration, expressing confidence that the President’s supporters in the region remained committed to his re-election. ‎ ‎“There is no panic and no going back in our support for Tinubu. The criticisms coming from the opposition will not stop us from voting for him in the North,” he said. ‎ ‎The APC chieftain urged party members to concentrate on strengthening their structures, maintaining regular contact with voters and seeking their support ahead of the elections. ‎ ‎“Don’t allow the opposition criticism to distract you, concentrate on strengthening the party structures and maintaining regular contact with voters and seek their support ahead of the elections,” he said. ‎ ‎He described the opposition’s criticism as part of political manoeuvring ahead of the 2027 elections, arguing that hostile political rhetoric alone could not erase Tinubu’s support across northern communities. ‎ ‎According to him, voters in the region were increasingly concerned about issues affecting their daily lives, including economic recovery, security, infrastructure development, employment and national stability. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso maintained that the policies, programmes and achievements of the Tinubu administration since assuming office had continued to strengthen confidence among supporters. ‎ ‎He added that supporters of the President would intensify grassroots engagement across northern communities to communicate government policies and highlight what they considered the administration’s achievements. ‎ ‎The APC chieftain expressed confidence that the political coalition backing Tinubu would remain united and focused, adding that supporters were prepared to defend the administration’s record and seek another mandate. ‎ ‎He called on Tinubu’s supporters across northern Nigeria to remain committed, describing the 2027 elections as an opportunity to sustain ongoing government policies and programmes and give the President more time to consolidate his development agenda. ‎ The post Don’t allow opposition criticism to distract you – APC to supporters appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fashola urges grassroots mobilisation ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor and Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola, has urged All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders in the South-West to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and engage stakeholders across party lines to secure victory in the 2027 general elections. Fashola made the call on Tuesday at a strategic meeting of South-West political stakeholders held in Ikeja, Lagos. The meeting was attended by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, APC State Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, and other party leaders and zonal coordinators. Fashola outlined a strategy for unifying party structures and increasing voter turnout ahead of the elections. He urged participants from the six states in the zone to establish structured stakeholder engagement forums at three levels: state, local government and ward. Emphasising the need for inclusive engagement, he said stakeholders should not be limited to APC members but should include individuals and groups capable of influencing electoral outcomes across party lines. “A stakeholder is anyone who can impact election outcomes, spanning party lines, opposing caucuses, artisans and union members,” he said. Fashola, who is working with former Ondo State Governor Segun Mimiko, former Ekiti State Governor Segun Oni and Secretary Senator Fatai Buhari on the Presidential Campaign Council’s South-West strategy, said he would visit each state after the initial engagement forums had been established. He said the visits would provide opportunities to address local political concerns, respect the peculiarities of each state and escalate issues requiring national intervention. Describing politics as local, Fashola urged party leaders to reach out to newly registered voters and re-engage those who had become apathetic towards the electoral process. He also called on them to recognise the significance of the country’s North-South political rotation and take advantage of the prevailing political moment to strengthen the party’s electoral prospects. The meeting later went into a closed-door session, with a communiqué expected at the end of the deliberations for release to the media. item.title: ‘Uncle Sam, Osoba, others built Daily Times, I’m just a custodian’ — Anosike
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Chairman of Folio Media Group, owners of Daily Times of Nigeria, Fidelis Anosike, has described himself as a custodian of the newspaper, crediting its founding fathers and former leaders for building the institution into a major force in Nigeria’s history. Anosike spoke at the Daily Times Heroes Award in Lagos, where he said the newspaper’s legacy was built through the sacrifices and contributions of distinguished individuals, including Uncle Sam, Aremo Olusegun Osoba and Yemi Ogunbiyi. The event, themed ‘Honouring the Past, Shaping the Future’, brought together stakeholders to celebrate individuals who contributed to the growth and development of the newspaper. Anosike said Daily Times did not belong to him, stressing that his responsibility was to preserve its legacy and ensure its continued relevance. “When we talk about Daily Times, it doesn’t belong to me. Daily Times belongs to Uncle Sam, Osoba, Yemi Ogunbiyi, late Dele Cole and Chief Onyema Ugochukwu. They built Daily Times. “I’m just a custodian, and I’m one of the luckiest custodians you can ever find because all of them have rallied around us to make sure that we celebrate what we’re celebrating today and that we can actually shape the future,” he said. He noted that many of those who built the newspaper were in their 20s and 30s at the time, adding that their contributions extended beyond journalism to nation-building. Anosike also recalled that some former contributors and leaders of the newspaper went on to establish or strengthen other media organisations, citing Sam Amuka’s contribution to Vanguard. He said Daily Times played a significant role in shaping Nigeria’s national identity, arguing that its influence went beyond its status as a newspaper organisation. “Sometimes people think that Daily Times is a newspaper company. It started as a newspaper company, but Daily Times, the nation built it. Nigeria is not Nigeria today if there was no Daily Times,” he added. item.title: Security agencies rescue eight kidnap victims in Kaduna
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA – Security agencies, comprising the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Police Force and the Military, have rescued eight kidnap victims during coordinated operations in Kaduna State. The victims were rescued between October 31 and November 2, 2026, in intelligence-driven operations conducted in the Millennium City and Marabar Rido areas of Chikun Local Government Area, in collaboration with the Kaduna State Government. Addressing journalists at the DSS Command headquarters in Kaduna, the Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Rabiu, said the operations were part of sustained efforts to identify, disrupt and dismantle criminal networks responsible for repeated kidnappings in the areas. He said the communities had witnessed recurring abductions, raising concerns among residents and attracting public attention to the security situation. The rescued victims were identified as Jamila Muhammad, 27, wife of Abdulkadir Bello; Talatu Yakubu, 40; Yunana Bawa, 30; Calista Bishop, 27; Chidinma Onuwere, 36; Eucharia Obi, 41; Godiya Victor, 50; and an eight-year-old girl, Miracle Alex. The latest rescue came barely three weeks after security operatives freed Ahmad Zakka and members of his family from captivity on October 15, 2026. Rabiu said the successive operations demonstrated the determination of security agencies to secure the release of abducted persons and dismantle criminal networks operating across the state. He acknowledged the coordination provided by ONSA, the operational support of the Police, the intelligence contributions of the DSS and the involvement of the Military. The police commissioner also commended the Kaduna State Government, under Governor Uba Sani, for its cooperation and support in tackling kidnapping and banditry. He said the operations were in line with President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening national security and protecting lives and property through improved collaboration among security and intelligence agencies. Rabiu disclosed that security agencies were intensifying operations across the state, with additional personnel and equipment, including 30 operational vans and eight armoured personnel carriers, to be deployed to strengthen security and improve response to criminal activities. He noted that criminal groups often exploited the difficult terrain in parts of Kaduna State to launch attacks and evade security operatives. The commissioner urged residents to support security agencies by providing credible and actionable intelligence on the identities, activities and movements of suspected kidnappers and other criminal elements. He assured the public that information supplied would be treated confidentially and acted upon appropriately. Rabiu also called on traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders to support efforts to tackle insecurity. He urged media organisations to maintain responsible and professional report

item.title: Soludo approves remodelling of Upper Iweka
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – The Anambra State Executive Council has approved the remodelling of Upper Iweka, Onitsha, as part of the state government’s urban regeneration programme. The project is expected to transform the aesthetics, functionality and land use of the area, a major gateway into Anambra State. The Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the weekly State Executive Council meeting at the Government House, Awka. He said the remodelling would cover parks and other public spaces, giving the area a new look in line with the state government’s vision of a livable and prosperous homeland. Mefor added that a detailed master plan and design for the project would be unveiled soon. At the meeting, the council also directed the Anambra Road Traffic Management Agency (ARTMA) to issue a one-month notice to owners of abandoned vehicles on roads across the state to remove them. The commissioner said vehicles not removed after the expiration of the notice would be impounded, taken away and scrapped by the government. He explained that the measure was intended to eliminate road hazards, improve traffic flow and enhance the safety and appearance of roads across the state. The council also approved the commencement of the selection, placement and training of the third batch of the One Youth, Two Skills entrepreneurship programme. Mefor said the Ministry of Youth Development would announce the eligibility requirements and application procedures in due course. He recalled that two batches of the programme had been completed, with more than 13,000 youths trained, empowered and mentored in over 60 skill areas. According to him, more than 5,000 beneficiaries have become millionaires and are now training and empowering other young people under the programme’s pay-it-forward model. “The One Youth, Two Skills initiative remains a flagship youth empowerment programme of the Soludo administration aimed at creating a new tribe of skilled, productive and self-reliant youths,” Mefor said. item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage.
